claims.text: The Eclipse S-CORE project describes itself as an open-source core stack for Software Defined Vehicles, specifically targeting embedded high-performance ECUs.
claims.context: Project-stated scope, not independent adoption evidence.

claims.text: Across v0.2.0 through v0.6.4, release notes show a progression from safety manuals/component requirements and communication/persistency architecture through API/SOME-IP work, safety artefacts/platform testing, reference integration, and explicit module maturity classification.
claims.context: Synthesis of project-authored release notes; not a claim of certification or production deployment.

claims.text: The v0.6.0 release notes include a reference integration repository, platform integration tests, persistency safety analysis and multiple safety/tool-evaluation changes.
claims.context: Directly checkable entries in the official GitHub release notes.

claims.text: The v0.6.4 release notes include a decision record for module maturity classification using Release, Experimental and Preview categories.

limitations.text: Release notes are project-authored evidence of repository changes; they do not by themselves establish production deployment, interoperability, functional-safety certification or automotive-grade maturity.
The v0.1.0 release page provides a release and full-changelog link but no detailed release-note body, so its exact technical baseline is unresolved from this source alone.

unresolved_questions: What exact runtime/platform component baseline was delivered in v0.1.0 beyond the existence of the tag/release?
Which S-CORE components had production-grade or safety-qualified status at each release, as distinct from documentation/process maturity?

editorial.why_now_note: The retained releases span May 2025 through August 2026 and show rapid maturation of an open core-stack effort aimed at SDV high-performance ECUs.
editorial.rationale: The release series is a useful implementation-level trace of how an open automotive core platform accumulates communication, safety, integration and maturity mechanisms.
